newsitem.title: THAILAND: Dissident urges intl help to avoid civil war.
newsitem.headline: Dissident urges intl help to avoid civil war.

text.p: Cambodian opposition leader Sam Rainsy called on the international community on Sunday to help ensure civil war does not break out in his country.

"I think we cannot afford to remain idle. The country is heading for civil war, for political disintegration and chaos," Sam Rainsy told the Foreign Correspondents Club in Bangkok, capital of neighbouring Thailand.

"The only way to avoid a civil war is to ensure the organisation of free and fair elections," he said. "I appeal to the international community to intervene again in Cambodia... If we let the Cambodian election proceed alone the process will derail."
Sam Rainsy, who is due to return to Phnom Penh on Monday, has been out of Cambodia for five weeks, having left soon after a grenade attack killed 19 people at an opposition rally on March 30.

He said the government is now "paralysed" by infighting between the two co-prime ministers, Norodom Ranariddh of the royalist FUNCINPEC party and former communist Hun Sen of the Cambodian People's Party.

The two formed uneasy partnership after U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993 but tensions between the two leaders and their parties has now paralysed the coalition government and some analysts question whether preparations are moving ahead for elections planned for next year.
Sam Rainsy has blamed the recent violence on Hun Sen, who denies involvement, and has joined in an alliance with Ranariddh to challenge Hun Sen in the polls,

"It is not too late yet, but we don't have much time to lose," Sam Rainsy told the journalists' club. "In the next few weeks and months the situation will change, I think for the worse. If there is no prospect for free and fair elections the only alternative left would be for military intervention."
Sam Rainsy, who said 60 percent of Cambodia's expenditures were financed by international assistance, said he was not asking for more money.

He said he wanted the international community to build on the 1991 Paris Peace Accord and find a way to ensure that elections are held as promised in 1998. He called for an organised group of international observers to the election and assistance in setting up a voter's list to ensure the fairness of the polls.
"Asking for an election is not asking too much. This is the commitment made in Paris (in 1991) by all Cambodian factions."
Sam Rainsy said the March 30 grenade attack would not change his resolve or that of his Khmer Nation Party, although he said he feared for his safety and that of other opposition politicians.
"We do not intend to change whatsoever. On the contrary, we have to be firm and stick to our principles," he said.
